chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Abi Najran and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding two sisters: a man married one of them, then divorced her while she was pregnant, then he proposed to her sister, so he married them both before the divorced sister gave birth to her child. So he ordered that he separate from the second one until the divorced sister gives birth to her child, then he should propose to her and give her a dowry, [giving] two dowries.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying two sisters when one is pregnant from a previous marriage?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies the specific condition for 'jam' (simultaneous marriage) of two sisters, emphasizing that the prohibition persists as long as the first sister remains in the 'iddah' (waiting period) of her divorce, even if she is pregnant. The requirement for two distinct dowries underscores the legal independence of each marriage contract, a nuance highlighted in Shia jurisprudence to distinguish this case from the general prohibition found in the Quran. This precedent ensures that the marital bond with the first sister is fully dissolved before the second bond is established, preventing any overlap in rights.
